title: Piano ADSR as a real graph
summary: Real recorded note: attack spike, decay, sustain-ish release. Envelope is a function of time (energy vs t); derivative is instantaneous rate of change—what the ear is highly sensitive to.

title: Exponential decay ODE
summary: If energy loses a fixed fraction per unit time, Ė = −kE ⇒ E(t)=E₀e^{−kt}. Measured time constant ~0.61s for the example (energy to ~37%). Exponential vs linear fade: ‘breathing’ vs abrupt cut. Model is approximate (multi-string partials).

title: Partials / harmonic stack
summary: One piano note is a stack of partials at roughly integer frequency multiples; each can decay differently—Fourier content of a ‘single’ note. Silence is practical threshold, not mathematical zero of the exponential.
